content.text:
Fixed — Kane verifies green against the running app.

**The bug** (`target-app/src/App.tsx:22`): `useState(false)` hardcoded the theme on every mount, and the effect only ever wrote to `document.body.dataset.theme`. Nothing left the page, so every reload came back light.

**The fix**, three small changes:
- `readStoredTheme()` reads `kane-notes-theme` from `localStorage`, in a `try/catch` so private-mode or blocked-storage browsers fall back to light instead of throwing on first render.
- The state seeds from it lazily — `useState(readStoredTheme)` passes the function rather than calling it, so it reads storage once at mount instead of on every render.
- The existing theme effect now persists alongside applying the attribute, keeping the write on the same path that already owns the transition.

Note on one detail I left alone: the theme is applied in `useEffect`, which runs after first paint, so a reload technically shows one frame of light before dark lands. Killing that entirely needs an inline script in `index.html` to set the attribute before React boots, and `target-app/CLAUDE.md` scopes edits to `./src` — so I stayed inside the boundary. It's imperceptible in practice and doesn't affect the flow, but it's the reason there's no pre-paint theme set.
